subject: Stage redefinition + skillshare: Commit/Best Case/Pipeline changes
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sales Leadership <sales-leadership@redwood.com>, Sales Ops <sales-ops@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurements@acme.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Stage redefinition + skillshare: Commit/Best Case/Pipeline changes

Team —

Quick update and ask: we've finalized a small but important set of definition changes for our forecasting categories (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline). The goal is to reduce subjective commits and make it easier for finance and ops to trust the weekly numbers. Key changes are in the attached stage_definitions_v1.2.pdf. 

High level changes (summary):
- Commit: now requires either an executed PO/contract OR verbal approval + documented procurement contact + reconciliation note in Salesforce. No more warm-nod-only commits.
- Best Case: clearly defined as deals with pricing agreed but procurement or legal still outstanding.
- Pipeline: qualification and discovery (no pricing agreed).

Please do these three things by EOD Friday, Dec 3:
1) Update any deals you currently have in Commit that do not meet the new criteria (move to Best Case or Pipeline and add a short rationale in the deal notes).
2) Join one of the two live skillshare sessions (links below) where we'll walk through examples and Q&A.
3) Tag any deals you believe should be grandfathered with the label: stage-refactor-2026Q4.

Attachments: stage_definitions_v1.2.pdf (see folder link below)
Skillshare times (pick one):
- Tue Dec 1, 10:00–10:45 PT — live Q&A + walk-through (recorded)
- Wed Dec 2, 15:00–15:45 PT — example-centered session for AE/AMs

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abcd1234-stage-refactor
HubSpot reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/RDW-ACME-452

Why this matters: Finance wants higher fidelity for Commit so forecasting is actionable. Operations will automate rollups once teams standardize on these labels.

If you have open Commit deals that are purely verbal, flag them now — we'll review exceptions only for deals with signed paperwork incoming within 14 days.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for flagging. Decision from Ops + Finance after the skillshare: we will grandfather deals that meet BOTH of these criteria:
1) Customer has provided explicit verbal signoff (email or recorded call note) AND
2) Contract/PO is expected to land within 14 calendar days.

For grandfathered deals please: add the tag stage-refactor-2026Q4, put a 1–2 line reconciliation note on the deal (what's outstanding and expected date), and assign the owner to follow up. Deals that do not meet both criteria should be moved to Best Case.

Sales Ops will run the office hours and publish a short FAQ from common edge cases. Thanks to everyone who joined the sessions — we captured example language you can paste into notes in training_slides_v2.pptx.

If you need an exception after the 14-day review window, escalate to FinanceOps (financeops@redwood.com) with full context.

-Steph
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
